_meta.indication: ALTABAX is indicated for use in adults and pediatric patients aged 9 months and older for the topical treatment of impetigo due to Staphylococcus aureus (methicillin-susceptible isolates only) or Streptococcus pyogenes.

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, multi-center, placebo-controlled study; subjects received topical 1% SB-275833 ointment twice daily for 5 days or placebo ointment twice daily for 5 days in a 2:1 ratio.
pivotal_trials.population: Adult and pediatric subjects aged 9 months or greater with impetigo
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Clinical response (success or failure) at the end of therapy visit
pivotal_trials.n: 213 randomized subjects (140 SB-275833, 73 placebo); the ITTC analysis population was 210 (139 ALTABAX, 71 placebo).
pivotal_trials.result: At end of therapy, clinical success in the ITTC population was 85.6% with ALTABAX versus 52.1% with placebo (difference 33.5%; 95% CI 20.5, 46.5).

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, observer-blind (single-blind/observer-blinded), multi-center, active-controlled non-inferiority study; subjects received topical 1% SB-275833 ointment twice daily for 5 days or topical 2% sodium fusidate ointment three times daily for 7 days in a 2:1 ratio.
pivotal_trials.population: Adult and pediatric subjects aged 9 months or greater with impetigo. Note: the comparator sodium fusidate ointment is not an approved comparator, and the Division previously informed the sponsor that showing non-inferiority to a non-approved comparator could not serve as a pivotal study; this study served as supportive.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Clinical response (success or failure) at the end of therapy visit
pivotal_trials.result: At end of therapy, clinical success in the ITTC population was 94.8% with retapamulin (327/345) versus 90.1% with sodium fusidate (155/172); difference 4.7% (95% CI -0.4, 9.7). The study, reviewed as a superiority trial, failed to demonstrate superiority and was considered supportive only.

key_safety: The most common drug-related adverse reaction was application site irritation (≤2% of patients). Drug-related adverse events occurred in 5.5% (116/2,115) of retapamulin patients; the most common drug-related event with retapamulin was application site irritation (1.4%). For context, drug-related events occurred in 6.6% (54/819) with the cephalexin comparator and 2.8% (2/71) with placebo.
target_moa: Retapamulin is a semisynthetic pleuromutilin antibacterial that selectively inhibits bacterial protein synthesis by interacting at a site on the 50S subunit of the bacterial ribosome (involving ribosomal protein L3); it is bacteriostatic against S. aureus and S. pyogenes.

summary.text: ALTABAX (retapamulin) was submitted as a 505(b) NDA received June 12, 2006 under standard review, and was approved on the strength of one placebo-controlled pivotal study (TOC103469) with supportive data from study TOC100224; a deferred pediatric study (ages 2 months to 9 months) was required under PREA.

citations.quote: Please refer to your new drug application (NDA) dated June 12, 2006, received June 12, 2006, submitted under section 505(b) of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act for Altabax (retapamulin ointment), 1%.
PDURA due date: April 12, 2007Review Priority: Standard

The results from study 103469 and the supportive findings from study 100224 provide evidence of the efficacy of retapamulin for the treatment of impetigo due to methicillin-sensitive S. aureus or S. pyogenes in patients 9 months of age or older.
- Deferred pediatric study under PREA for the treatment of impetigo in pediatric patients ages 2 months to 9 months.
